candidates.lead: A printed page from a 1981 Lithuanian civil-defence training album, drawn and printed like the Soviet Grazhdanskaya Oborona wall charts of 1975-1985: dark-brown brush-and-ink outlines around every figure and object, matte gouache fills with soft shading, four-colour offset with a faint coarse halftone, muted inks of dusty blue, olive, ochre, brick red and grey-brown on light aged cream paper with a faint yellow cast. The light paper is the background: the main subject is drawn directly on it, its surroundings sketched in around it and fading into the paper, leaving open margins; insets are small ruled boxes on the same paper, each a clearly different moment or detail. Flat even diagram lighting, a quiet nostalgic warmth. People are ordinary Lithuanians of 1981, anonymous types with correct natural proportions: fair skin, ash-blond to light-brown hair, grey or blue-grey eyes, broad-cheeked oval faces, straight noses, calm closed mouths, austere and plainly handsome. Men side-parted or cropped, some moustached, working men in flat caps; younger women lean, hair straight or faintly waved; older women with set or curled hair or a cotton headscarf; clothes plain and loosely cut, in brown, olive, dusty blue, grey and dull red, chosen for the setting and occasion. In a group, heads turn at varied natural angles as in a documentary photograph, most people looking at their task or at each other, one or two facing the viewer with eyes resting just past the viewer's shoulder; a lone figure stands near-frontal, face turned only a little, eyes just past the viewer's shoulder.
candidates.suffix: Finish: muted offset print on light aged cream paper with a faint yellow cast, brush-ink outlines, soft shading, correct proportions. Group heads at varied natural angles, one or two facing the viewer with eyes just past the viewer's shoulder; a lone figure near-frontal. Every inset a clearly different moment, all in the same ruled frame. Diagram arrows and callouts in solid black ink.

setting_line_hook.field: deck_builder SETTING[<card_key>] -> appended after the staging line as 'Setting: ...'
setting_line_hook.format: One sentence naming a real Lithuanian place as it stood in 1981, with two or three visible identifying details and nothing written; e.g. 'Setting: Kaunas, Laisvės alėja near the Soboras, lime trees and the 1930s modernist facades.'
setting_line_hook.coverage: owner asked for roughly 2/3 to 3/4 of cards; the researcher's bank fills it; cards without a bank entry get no Setting line
setting_line_hook.guard: the setting must never compete with the target word (INSET_MEANING_RULE applies); for object cards the setting goes in an inset, not around the main subject

FIGURE_DRESS.worker: Any people who appear are working men and women in plain muted blue-grey work jackets and trousers, the men in flat cloth caps, with black kirza-style work boots.
FIGURE_DRESS.professional: Any people who appear are dressed for their profession and setting: a doctor or nurse in a white coat, with a small red cross on the medical kit or the clinic front; a teacher in a modest jacket or dress with pupils present at their desks; a shop assistant in a white smock; a uniformed officer in plain service uniform.
FIGURE_DRESS.civilian: Any people who appear are ordinary Lithuanian civilians in plain everyday clothes of 1981, dressed for the setting and the weather: shirts, cardigans, simple dresses and headscarves indoors and on the street; coats, caps and hats outdoors in cold weather.
FIGURE_DRESS.formal: Any people who appear are ordinary Lithuanians in their Sunday best for church, a wedding or a celebration: men in dark suits with a white shirt and tie, women in modest good dresses or skirts with a cardigan, a small hat or a fine headscarf, children neatly dressed.
FIGURE_DRESS.routing_note: deck_builder: route bažnyčia, vestuvės, šventė, koncertas, teatras and similar occasion cards to 'formal'; medical cards to 'professional' (red cross is now in the class text, the per-card staging line can drop it).

rule_blocks.INSET_RULE: Include just 2 to 3 small supporting inset panels, all drawn in the same thin ruled frame on the same paper, each showing a clearly different moment, object or angle from the others and from the main picture. Keep them clean and uncluttered.
rule_blocks.MOTION_STRIP_RULE: The motion strip shows one figure in three clearly different phases, left to right: first standing with both feet together and arms at the sides; second with the LEFT foot forward and the right arm swung forward; third with the RIGHT foot forward and the left arm swung forward. The three frames read as one continuous movement.
rule_blocks.PLAUSIBILITY_RULE: Every object, tool and fixture is complete, attached and in working order: a well-sweep stands over its timber well-head, hanging utensils hang from a proper rack or wall hooks, doorways and corridors stay clear and passable, furniture rests on the floor against a wall, tools are held in a usable grip, and a resting or sleeping animal is visibly alive and at ease, curled up with eyes closed and ears relaxed.
rule_blocks.ARROW_RULE: Any arrow or callout, drawn in solid black ink, points only at the subject the card teaches or at the direction of its motion.
rule_blocks.NO_TEXT_RULE: UNCHANGED in production. Per-card text only through _exact_text_rule under the text pilot (see text_policy).

text_policy.status: NO_TEXT_RULE stays in production until the pilot passes

pilot.selection: cards where lettering teaches: mokytojas/mokykla (board arithmetic '7 x 8 = 56', 'S = v t'), parduotuvė/pirkti (sign PARDUOTUVĖ; price tags as decided below), ligoninė (sign LIGONINĖ), duona (sign DUONA), knyga/biblioteka (two or three interwar spines: 'ALTORIŲ ŠEŠĖLY', 'METAI', 'DĖDĖS IR DĖDIENĖS'), laikraštis (masthead only), kalendorius, laiškas (address block of three short lines), bankas, paštas
pilot.mechanism: use the existing _exact_text_rule(spec, exclude) per card; the spec names the EXACT string(s), uppercase where a sign would be, in the muted period sign-painting or chalk style; at most two strings per card; the target word itself is still never written (exclude clause)
pilot.language_rules: Lithuanian only, with correct diacritics (ą č ę ė į š ų ū ž); period-plausible wording; formulas and numbers true for the 1981 secondary curriculum (arithmetic tables, S = v t, F = m a, H2O, NaCl, 1 kg = 1000 g); interwar titles and spellings allowed as the owner's deliberate anachronism; currency on price tags is an OWNER DECISION (counterfactual free Lithuania 1981: litas/centai 'Lt / ct' vs period rubles) and is left blank until decided
pilot.whitelist: researcher compiles style_lab/research/text_whitelist.csv: card_key, string, style (sign/chalk/spine/label), source; nothing outside the whitelist is ever requested
pilot.qa_gate: (1) automatic read-back: a vision model transcribes every lettering region; the transcript must equal the whitelisted string exactly, diacritics included; (2) zero stray lettering anywhere else on the card (the usual check); (3) human check of period plausibility by the owner. Pass threshold for lifting the rule on a card CLASS: >= 90 % of text instances exact across the 40 pilot renders and 0 stray-text cards. On pass, that class keeps using _exact_text_rule with whitelisted strings; NO_TEXT_RULE remains the default for every other card. On fail, the class stays wordless.

model_decision.evidence_for_sunburst: F6 roll: 1st in 3 of 4 rounds (eiti, duona, lėtas; 'best colour', 'all details right', 'wonderful card'); its paper is the owner's anchor; 3.3x cheaper ($7 vs $23 for 520 cards), ~2x faster; proportions correct on every F5/F6 draw.
model_decision.evidence_against: n = 4, all single-subject cards; its earlier losses were on multi-person and scene cards (full-bleed drift, 'flat/bland', klubas Western, minia target-word drift) and on gaze (paltas 'looking too far away' in this roll); it renders the bands a brighter scarlet than gpt-image-2's dark red, so mixing models would be visible across the deck.
model_decision.decision: Undetermined on current data. Settle it in the 30-card production spot-check by dual-rendering: 30 cards x both models (gpt-image-2 $1.32 + Sunburst $0.41), stratified 10 multi-person/scene (F6.1D), 10 single-figure verbs/persons, 10 objects/animals/clothing. Blind pairwise with ship flags. Sunburst becomes the production model if it wins >= 60 % overall AND >= 50 % of the multi-person/scene stratum AND its plausibility-glitch rate is <= gpt-image-2's; otherwise gpt-image-2. Whichever wins renders all 520 and everything after; add 'deep dark brick-red bands' to BARS_RULE if Sunburst wins, and re-measure paper on its first 30.
model_decision.cost_note: Dual-rendering the spot-check costs $1.73; a wrong model choice costs a $23 re-render or a visibly inconsistent deck.

qa_expectation: Style is settled; remaining failures are content/plausibility (5 of 28 A/Y images, ~18 %). Budget a 20 % re-roll rate in production QA; re-roll triggers: plausibility glitch, duplicate insets, same-foot motion strip, inconsistent inset frames, missing pupils/cross/occasion dress, target word unclear.
